FJ3176.name: Atlas
FJ3176.details: First cervical vertebra; ring-shaped, lacking body and spinous process; lateral masses carry occipital condyles above and axis below; vertebral artery grooves its posterior arch.
FJ3176.clinicalCondition: Jefferson burst fracture — axial load through the skull splits the ring, displacing lateral masses outward.
FJ3176.clinicalScenario: A 22-year-old dives into shallow water and strikes his head; he has severe neck pain and CT shows a four-part burst fracture of C1.

FJ3177.name: Axis
FJ3177.details: Second cervical vertebra; its odontoid process (dens) projects upward and is held against the atlas by the transverse ligament, forming the pivot for head rotation.
FJ3177.clinicalCondition: Odontoid fracture — elderly falls; type II fractures risk nonunion and spinal cord injury.
FJ3177.clinicalScenario: An 82-year-old woman falls face-first at home; CT reveals a type II dens fracture and she is fitted with a rigid cervical collar.

FJ3178.name: Body of sternum
FJ3178.details: Flat central segment of the sternum between manubrium and xiphoid process; articulates with costal cartilages two to seven; overlies the heart and great vessels.
FJ3178.clinicalCondition: Sternal fracture — blunt steering-wheel trauma; a marker for underlying cardiac and pulmonary contusion.
FJ3178.clinicalScenario: A driver whose chest struck the steering wheel has midsternal bruising and pain; CT shows a transverse sternal fracture and troponin is checked.

FJ2440.name: Cricoid cartilage
FJ2440.details: Signet-ring-shaped hyaline cartilage of the larynx at C6 level; the only complete ring of the airway; connected above to thyroid cartilage by cricothyroid membrane.
FJ2440.clinicalCondition: Post-intubation subglottic stenosis — pressure injury at this narrow, rigid ring scars and narrows the airway.
FJ2440.clinicalScenario: A child extubated after prolonged ventilation develops progressive stridor; endoscopy shows subglottic narrowing precisely at the cricoid level.

FJ2769.name: Cricoid cartilage
FJ2769.details: Surface landmark at C6: here pharynx becomes esophagus and larynx becomes trachea; the carotid pulse is palpated against the adjacent transverse process of C6.
FJ2769.clinicalCondition: Cricoid pressure (Sellick maneuver) — compresses the esophagus during rapid-sequence induction, reducing aspiration risk.
FJ2769.clinicalScenario: During emergency intubation of a vomiting trauma patient, an assistant applies firm cricoid pressure while the anesthetist secures the airway with a cuffed tube.

FJ3182.name: Distal phalanx of left big toe
FJ3182.details: Terminal bone of the hallux; supports nail and pulp; flexor and extensor hallucis longus tendons insert around its base, aiding balance and push-off.
FJ3182.clinicalCondition: Tuft fracture with subungual hematoma — crush injury traps painful blood beneath the nail.
FJ3182.clinicalScenario: A warehouse worker drops a crate on his left foot; X-ray shows a tuft fracture of the great toe with a tense subungual hematoma.

FJ3188.name: Distal phalanx of left thumb
FJ3188.details: Stout terminal thumb bone; flexor pollicis longus inserts palmarly and extensor pollicis longus dorsally; essential for pinch, grip, and opposition.
FJ3188.clinicalCondition: Tuft fracture with nail-bed injury — crush impact is the commonest mechanism in manual workers.
FJ3188.clinicalScenario: A joiner strikes his left thumb with a hammer; X-ray shows a tuft fracture and the lacerated nail bed is sutured after removing the nail.

FJ3259.name: Left femur
FJ3259.details: Longest and strongest bone; its head sits in the acetabulum at a neck angle near 125 degrees, the shaft bears the linea aspera, and the condyles form the knee.
FJ3259.clinicalCondition: Femoral neck fracture — in the elderly, displaced fractures threaten the head's blood supply, causing avascular necrosis.
FJ3259.clinicalScenario: An 84-year-old falls at home and cannot bear weight; her left leg lies shortened and externally rotated, and X-ray confirms a fractured neck of femur.

FJ3262.name: Left humerus
FJ3262.details: Upper-arm bone; head articulates with the glenoid, the radial nerve winds in the spiral groove against its midshaft, and trochlea and capitulum form the elbow.
FJ3262.clinicalCondition: Midshaft fracture with radial nerve palsy — the nerve's groove contact makes wrist drop a classic sign.
FJ3262.clinicalScenario: A man with a left humeral shaft fracture cannot extend his wrist or fingers; a cock-up splint is fitted for radial nerve palsy.

FJ3237.name: Left clavicle
FJ3237.details: S-shaped strut linking sternum to scapula, first bone to ossify; the subclavian vessels and brachial plexus pass behind its middle third.
FJ3237.clinicalCondition: Midshaft clavicle fracture — among the commonest fractures, from falls onto the shoulder.
FJ3237.clinicalScenario: A cyclist thrown over the handlebars has a deformed, tender left mid-clavicle with a drooping shoulder; X-ray confirms a displaced midshaft fracture.

FJ2564.name: Stomach
FJ2564.details: J-shaped muscular reservoir between esophagus and duodenum with fundus, body, antrum and pylorus; vagal and enteric control of acid secretion and peristaltic mixing.
FJ2564.clinicalCondition: Perforated gastric ulcer — sudden acid spillage causes board-like abdominal rigidity and free subdiaphragmatic gas.
FJ2564.clinicalScenario: An NSAID user collapses with abrupt severe epigastric pain and a rigid abdomen; erect chest film shows gas under the diaphragm.

FJ2561.name: Spleen
FJ2561.details: Largest lymphoid organ, sheltered under the left 9th–11th ribs; filters blood, removes worn red cells, mounts immune responses; supplied by the splenic artery, draining to portal vein.
FJ2561.clinicalCondition: Splenic rupture — blunt trauma causes intraperitoneal hemorrhage, sometimes delayed.
FJ2561.clinicalScenario: After falling from a height, a man becomes hypotensive with left shoulder-tip pain; CT shows a splenic laceration with hemoperitoneum.

FJ1895.name: Pancreas
FJ1895.details: Retroperitoneal gland at L1–L2 with head cradled by the duodenum, body crossing the aorta, and tail reaching the splenic hilum; combines exocrine acini with endocrine islets.
FJ1895.clinicalCondition: Acute pancreatitis — autodigestion from gallstones or alcohol causing epigastric pain radiating to the back.
FJ1895.clinicalScenario: A man with heavy alcohol use has severe epigastric pain boring through to his back, vomiting and a markedly raised lipase.

FJ2563.name: Esophagus
FJ2563.details: Muscular tube from cricopharyngeus (C6) to cardia (T11), about 25 cm, with constrictions at cricoid, aortic arch/bronchus and diaphragmatic hiatus; lower sphincter prevents reflux.
FJ2563.clinicalCondition: Esophageal carcinoma — progressive dysphagia, solids before liquids, with marked weight loss.
FJ2563.clinicalScenario: A 68-year-old smoker reports three months of worsening dysphagia and 10 kg weight loss; endoscopy reveals a malignant mid-esophageal stricture.

FJ2817.name: Gallbladder
FJ2817.details: Pear-shaped reservoir under the right liver lobe storing and concentrating bile; fundus, body and neck, with Hartmann pouch near the neck where stones impact.
FJ2817.clinicalCondition: Acute cholecystitis — cystic duct stone obstruction causing right upper quadrant pain and Murphy's sign.
FJ2817.clinicalScenario: A woman has constant right upper quadrant pain, fever and arrest of inspiration on palpation after a fatty meal, confirming acute cholecystitis.

FJ3149.name: Urinary bladder
FJ3149.details: Pelvic urine reservoir with a smooth trigone and detrusor muscle wall; the neck is guarded by the internal sphincter; parasympathetics (S2–4) drive voiding.
FJ3149.clinicalCondition: Bladder carcinoma — transitional cell tumors classically present with painless hematuria.
FJ3149.clinicalScenario: An elderly smoker with painless visible hematuria has a papillary tumor on the bladder's lateral wall at cystoscopy.

FJ3145.name: Left kidney
FJ3145.details: Retroperitoneal organ at about T11–L2, slightly higher than the right; hilum transmits vein, artery, and pelvis; related to spleen, pancreatic tail, and colon.
FJ3145.clinicalCondition: Renal cell carcinoma — classically hematuria, flank pain, and a palpable mass.
FJ3145.clinicalScenario: A 60-year-old smoker with painless gross hematuria has an enhancing mass in the upper pole of the left kidney on CT.

FJ3147.name: Right kidney
FJ3147.details: Retroperitoneal organ lying slightly lower than the left because of the liver; hilum transmits vein, artery, pelvis; related to liver, duodenum, and hepatic flexure.
FJ3147.clinicalCondition: Renal trauma — blunt injury can lacerate the kidney causing hematuria and hematoma.
FJ3147.clinicalScenario: A footballer kicked in the right loin develops gross hematuria; CT shows a right renal laceration with perinephric hematoma.

FJ3139.name: Prostate
FJ3139.details: Fibromuscular gland below the bladder neck surrounding the prostatic urethra; peripheral zone (cancer-prone) and transition zone; adds secretions to semen; palpable per rectum.
FJ3139.clinicalCondition: Benign prostatic hyperplasia — transition-zone growth obstructs outflow causing nocturia and weak stream.
FJ3139.clinicalScenario: A 70-year-old with nocturia and hesitancy has a smooth, enlarged prostate on rectal examination and mildly raised PSA.

FJ1796.name: Pituitary gland
FJ1796.details: Pea-sized gland in the sella turcica, stalk-linked to the hypothalamus; anterior lobe secretes GH, prolactin, ACTH, TSH, LH/FSH; posterior lobe releases ADH and oxytocin.
FJ1796.clinicalCondition: Pituitary adenoma — prolactinoma causes amenorrhea-galactorrhea; large tumors compress the optic chiasm.
FJ1796.clinicalScenario: A woman with amenorrhea and milky nipple discharge has a pituitary macroadenoma pressing on the optic chiasm on MRI.

FJ3129.name: Left adrenal gland
FJ3129.details: Crescentic gland capping the left kidney; cortex has glomerulosa, fasciculata, and reticularis zones around a medulla; drains via the left adrenal vein to the renal vein.
FJ3129.clinicalCondition: Conn syndrome — aldosterone-secreting adenoma causes hypertension with hypokalemia.
FJ3129.clinicalScenario: A young hypertensive with low potassium and metabolic alkalosis has a 1.5 cm left adrenal adenoma on CT.

FJ3130.name: Right adrenal gland
FJ3130.details: Pyramidal gland atop the right kidney, related to the IVC and liver; its short central vein drains directly into the IVC, a surgical hazard.
FJ3130.clinicalCondition: Pheochromocytoma — medullary tumor secretes catecholamines causing paroxysmal hypertension and palpitations.
FJ3130.clinicalScenario: A man with episodic headache, sweating, palpitations, and blood pressure of 220/120 has a right adrenal mass on CT.

FJ2422.name: Cavity of left ventricle
FJ2422.details: Chamber of the left ventricle that receives blood from the left atrium and ejects it into the aorta through the aortic valve.
FJ2422.clinicalCondition: Left ventricular failure — reduced ejection fraction causes pulmonary edema and dyspnea.
FJ2422.clinicalScenario: A patient with ischemic cardiomyopathy presents with orthopnea and bilateral basal crackles from left ventricular failure.

FJ2423.name: Cavity of right ventricle
FJ2423.details: Chamber of the right ventricle that receives venous blood from the right atrium and pumps it into the pulmonary trunk.
FJ2423.clinicalCondition: Right ventricular infarction — can accompany inferior MI and cause hypotension with clear lungs.
FJ2423.clinicalScenario: After an inferior STEMI, a patient is hypotensive with elevated JVP and clear lung fields, suggesting right ventricular involvement.

FJ2428.name: Wall of ventricle
FJ2428.details: Muscular wall of the cardiac ventricles responsible for generating systolic pressure to eject blood.
FJ2428.clinicalCondition: Myocardial infarction — coronary occlusion causes ischemic necrosis of ventricular muscle.
FJ2428.clinicalScenario: A man with crushing central chest pain and ST elevation has troponin rise from acute myocardial infarction of the ventricular wall.
